title: Bootstrap npm package ownership and trusted publishing
description:
The absent npm package/scope is created at pre-v1, verified, stripped of bootstrap credentials, and bound to trusted publishing through the already authority-owned protected environment.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An authorized package owner confirms the @erankavija scope and package name, packs and clean-install/protocol-smokes the current pre-v1 tarball, then runs npm publish <that-tarball> --access public exactly once with a narrowly scoped temporary credential and required owner authentication.
- [hard] REQ-02: Unauthenticated npm view plus clean registry install proves public visibility/integrity; the worker consumes the authority leaf's documented existing `npm-publish` environment identity without creating/editing any GitHub environment, then binds npm's trusted publisher to the exact repository, orchestration-owned direct-publish workflow filename, and that environment with direct publish allowed.
- [hard] REQ-03: Read-only verification proves authority-owned npm-publish permits only exact v1 tag execution, contains no App key, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, npm token, GHCR/GitHub secret, or final-release credential, and is isolated from candidate-tag/final-release. A pre-v1 staged-publish/2FA proof is optional npm-side evidence outside the v1 chain.
- [hard] REQ-04: Package access requires 2FA and disallows tokens, the temporary bootstrap credential is revoked, and evidence records revocation plus exact direct-publish OIDC binding; actual OIDC publish proof occurs on the transition-guarded v1 operation.
- [hard] REQ-05: Bootstrap uses only pre-v1, never reserves/publishes/stages 1.0.0, and proves npm-publish configuration before v1 tooling completes.

## Notes

Blast radius: npm package/scope metadata, bootstrap evidence/credential revocation, and npm-side trusted-publisher binding only; the authority-owned GitHub environment/configuration and orchestration workflow YAML are read-only inputs.
